## 1. What was read

**763 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **234** records (23% of the 997 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 460 | 122 | 75 | 328 | 12 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -34%, sysbio -50%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 163, Nature 108, JAMA 100, Science 97, Lancet 54, Bioinformatics 48.

## 3. The evidence that moved it








**A hospital-scale language model and a journal-scale argument about hype, in the
same four weeks.** [37286606](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37286606/)
(*Nature*) trains a language model on one health system's own notes and drives
several unrelated clinical predictions off a single backbone — the transfer step
`foundation-models` rests on, done inside a hospital rather than on a benchmark.
In the same month *JAMA* runs [37410477](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37410477/)
with hype in its title, beside pieces on chatbot privacy
[37410449](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37410449/), liability
[37410497](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37410497/) and the regulatory gap
[37410482](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37410482/), and a letter scoring a
generative model against a diagnostic challenge
[37318797](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37318797/). The thread reads +1 / −1
for the month; that is not indecision, it is two literatures publishing past each
other. Worth separating what these are: every AI item in the month is a model
that answers or predicts. Nothing in 997 titles is an agent that acts.

**Three papers in one journal issue make neurotransmitters the shared currency,
which is what the thread actually claims.** *Immunity* publishes gut lipids
setting peripheral serotonin release through CD1d
[37354904](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37354904/), a serotonin metabolite
recruiting eosinophils through GPR35
[37279752](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37279752/), and enteric GABA driving
innate gut defence [37437538](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37437538/).
Separately [37380778](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37380778/) (*Nature*) has
neuronal activity remote from the tumour driving glioma progression through
SEMA4F. `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` takes its largest gain of the quarter, and
takes it on the mechanism claim rather than on the topic.

**The atlas layer and the assay layer moved together, and one of them says they
are not interchangeable.** *Nature* runs three spatially resolved human organ
atlases in one issue — kidney [37468583](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37468583/),
intestine [37468586](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37468586/), maternal–fetal
interface [37468587](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37468587/) — with cardiac
niches [37438528](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37438528/) beside them, and
*Nature Methods* adds gene expression and chromatin accessibility profiled in the
same tissue section [37231265](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37231265/).
Against that, [37336949](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37336949/) recovers
multiway chromatin contacts Hi-C does not return, flagged by its own News & Views
[37336950](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37336950/). The output format is
consolidating faster than the assays feeding it agree with each other.

**Grade rather than novelty: engineered cells reach a randomised comparison
outside CD19.** [37272512](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37272512/) (*NEJM*)
tests a BCMA-directed CAR T product against standard care in myeloma. It is the
strongest single piece of evidence in the month for `cell-therapy`, and the
thread still closes the month at −1 net, because two refutations landed on it in
the same four weeks (section 4). Two detection results land on `interception`: a
multi-cancer test measured in symptomatic patients referred for investigation
rather than in a screening population
[37352875](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37352875/), and microbial metabolites
proposed as markers of an anal precancer
[37464040](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37464040/).

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[37264229](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37264229/) (*Nat Immunol*) — how much
the CD94/NKG2-HLA-E axis restrains effector cells is set by an HLA class I signal
peptide polymorphism. The shape of this is what matters: not that a target
failed, but that the size of what blockade could recover belongs to the patient
rather than to the drug. `next-gen-checkpoints` records nothing of this kind; its
whole ledger is which nominated targets reached a trial.

[37392737](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37392737/) (*Immunity*) —
TCR-independent 4-1BB signalling pushes exhausted CD8 T cells into proliferation
and terminal differentiation. The sign on an agonist target is inverted.

[37011008](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37011008/) (*Cancer Discov*) — type I
interferon signalling through EGR2 drives CAR T cells into intrinsic dysfunction.
The failure sits inside the engineered cell, not in the tumour it was aimed at.

[37247626](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37247626/) (*Lancet*) — early-phase
CAR T trials against novel target antigens are argued to report activity without
a stable denominator. A reporting refutation rather than a biological one, and
the only one of its kind this month.

### (b) Method credibility

Two cards, and the ratio needs saying out loud before section 2's `crisis` is
misread. This thread is a ledger of things found unreliable; every card that can
land on it refutes by construction, so +0 / −16 is the shape of the instrument,
not a measurement of collapse. Read the volume and the target of the audit, never
the sign.

[37349538](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37349538/) (*Nat Med*, with its News &
Views [37400641](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37400641/)) — variants published
as pathogenic for premature ovarian insufficiency show little penetrance in an
unselected population. The gene–disease calls do not survive contact with a
denominator.

[37224537](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37224537/) (*NAR*) — disrupting the
RNA–RNA contacts a published SPLASH map assigned to influenza genome packaging
does not produce the defect that map predicts. A specific published map, tested
and not confirmed.

Uncarded but worth the note, because of where in the stack it sits:
[37449901](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37449901/) (*Bioinformatics*) offers a
test of whether the populations reported from single-cell RNA-seq are
significantly different at all. The audit has reached the basic unit of analysis.
